why: This is the textbook exact-match problem for the week's Strings: KMP / Z / hashing. Build the KMP failure table for needle, then scan haystack once. The first time the matched length reaches len(needle), return the start index.
hints: Comparing the needle at every start is O(n*m), which is too slow at 10^5 by 10^5 in the worst case (e.g. 'aaaa...b').
KMP precomputes, for each prefix of needle, its longest proper prefix that is also a suffix. On a mismatch you fall back to that instead of restarting.
Build fail[] in O(m), scan haystack in O(n), and when k == m return i - m + 1. Return 0 for an empty needle and -1 if there is no match.
pitfalls: An empty needle returns 0, even for an empty haystack.
A needle longer than the haystack gives -1.
Return the start index, i - m + 1, not the end index.
